title: Falls and injury prevention in the elderly
bottleneck: Falls are the leading cause of injury death in older adults, driven by sarcopenia, balance-system decline, polypharmacy, and home hazards, but prevention is fragmented across geriatrics, physiotherapy, and public health with no accountable owner. Most interventions are tested in the relatively healthy, not the frailest who fall most.
why_it_blocks: A single hip fracture frequently ends independent living and starts a terminal decline cascade. Falls are among the most preventable causes of lost healthspan, yet prevention remains an unfunded afterthought.
current_state: Exercise programs (tai chi, balance training), medication review, and home modification reduce fall risk modestly. No pharmacological strategy addresses the underlying musculoskeletal and neurological decline. Multifactorial programs combining balance training, medication review, and home modification show the best results, though the frailest patients who need them most are rarely enrolled in trials.
